description: Match OCR length, allow up to two complete neighbouring words and any clipped words; block a second complete line or total vertical padding greater than 1.5 target-line heights.
normaliser: Long and short sides of the existing measured candidate_text_box, not x-height inferred from glyph widths. Exact quarter-turns leave this ratio unchanged.
calibration: Same 412 geometry-qualified calibration lines from the original 64 calibration books; no review labels or example-specific overrides in fitting. Same 163 qualified evaluation lines for comparable prediction metrics.
validation: Primary scoring uses the explicit current Space-bar ratings. Older 216 visual references remain a separate historical benchmark. This is post-review development, not a new blind audit.
backend: Rust calibration and prediction; existing Python detector supplies native geometry; no fallback
limits: Current boxes are existing target-component envelopes; native source-context whole-word evidence is an experimental geometric proxy
Whole-word groups and entire printed rows are different; local complete bands alone do not prove a complete second line
Any unresolved neighbour count remains UNCERTAIN; a decisive length, full-line, word-count or padding failure still produces DROP
Top plus bottom padding exceeding 1.5 line heights means segment height greater than 2.5 line heights
Historical frozen policies, model fits, labels and reader answers remain unchanged
The 16 Sol diagnostic crops were selected from owner-reviewed development cases; 15 had no complete neighbouring words and one was ambiguous. No fresh blind audit is claimed

The reconciled measured contexts currently contain zero positive whole-neighbour-word counts: the one-word and two-word allowance has synthetic boundary coverage only, not native positive-case qualification
